title: Definition
body_md:
The Sobolev space $W^{k,p}(M)$ is the completion of $C^p_k(M)$ with respect to the norm
$$\left\lVertu\right\rVert_{W^{k,p}}=\sum_{j=0}^{k}\Big(\int_M|\nabla^ju|^pdV\Big)^{1/p}.$$

title: Definition
body_md:
\cite{YAU75}
A $C^2$-function $u:M\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ is said to be harmonic if $\Delta u=0$. The function $u$ is called subharmonic (resp. superharmonic) if $\Delta \geq 0$ (resp. $\Delta u\leq 0$).

title: Theorem
body_md: There does not exist any non-trivial Killing potential $u\in C^2(M)$ in a complete Riemannian manifold $M$ with $Ric_M\geq cg$ for some constant $c>0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose $u\in C^2(M)$ is a non-trivial Killing potential. Now Hessian of $u$ vanishes \cite{CM99}. Since $u$ is a Killing potential so $u$ is harmonic function \cite{CM99}. Hence using Bochner's formula we get
$$ rac{1}{2}\Delta|
abla u|^2=|Hess(u)|^2+Ric(
abla u,
abla u)=Ric(
abla u,
abla u).$$
Again $Ric_M\geq cg$ implies that
$$\Delta |
abla u|^2\geq 2cg(
abla u,
abla u)=2c|
abla u|^2.$$
Since $u$ is Killing potential so $
abla u$ is covariant constant field \cite{CM99}, i.e., $
abla_ X(
abla u)=0 \quad  orall X\in \chi(M)$, which implies that $g(
abla u,
abla u)=C,$ for some constant $C> 0$. Hence $\Delta |
abla u|^2=0$ and it leads to a contradiction. Hence $u$ is constant.

title: Lemma
body_md:
\cite[Corollary 2]{BN08}
A complete Riemannian manifold $M$ of negative definite Ricci curvature has no nontrivial Killing fields of constant length.
head: environment

title: Corollary
body_md: If a complete Riemannian manifold $M$ admits a Killing potential $u\in C^\infty(M)$, then $Ric(\nabla u,\nabla u)_p=0\ \forall p\in M$.

body_md: Suppose $(M,g)$ is a complete non-compact Riemannian manifold with $Ric_M>-K$. If there is non-positive harmonic function $u\in C^2(M)$ satisfying (\ref{eq6}) for some positive constant $c$, then $u$ is constant. Hence $M$ satisfies $Ric\geq cg.$

title: Corollary
body_md: Let $M$ be a complete Riemannian manifold with $Ric_M>-K$. If there is a convex function $u\in C^2(M)$ which is bounded below and $|\nabla u|\in L^1(M)$ and also satisfies (\ref{eq6}), then there is a geodesic $\gamma:[0,\infty)\rightarrow M$, where $u$ takes the form (\ref{eq9}).

title: Proof
body_md: The convexity of $u$ implies that $u$ is subharmonic \cite{GW71}. Yau \cite{YAU76} proved that any subharmonic function $u\in C^2(M)$ with integrable norm on a complete Riemannian manifold is harmonic. Hence this corollary follows from Theorem \ref{th1}.
